# x86_avx.py cases where Rosetta and an x86 CPU differ: what it left (docs/macos/avx-data/silicon_overrides.py writes this file). One corpus line per family run on the x86 CPU, an AMD EPYC 9V74 (raven-macos-bench run 44502534716, assembled with clang as here; dump sha256 bc3ce25a2ec75c4fbe93f2b1dce131d64481a0e9323eb70f3c3e36609acc141a): the tests refuse the file when a family's cases or Rosetta's results change.
# Earlier runs: an AMD EPYC 7763 (run 44501136642) and an EPYC 9V74 (run 44499294363) gave the same results for the families they had. An Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C (run 44500206597, dump sha256 37b9cf0cca10f7637359a6b9f4038e75c67ac913423a83c8aff9da653fdcdcf8) agrees with Rosetta in the strings family, as the EPYCs do, and differs from the AMD runs in one dpps case (#7786, NaN lanes), not applied here: the AMD EPYC stays the reference.
